content.title: Mullen Automotive Rebrands To Bollinger Innovations
content.summary: Mullen Automotive (NASDAQ:MULN) stock dropped on Thursday as it announced it would officially change its name to Bollinger Innovations, effective July 28, 2025. On the same day, the company’s common stock will begin trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the new ticker symbol BINI. The CUSIP number for the stock will remain unchanged. content.title: California EV maker to consolidate with Bollinger Motors in Michigan under new name
content.summary: Mullen Automotive is betting heavy on Bollinger Motors, consolidating operations with the electric truck startup and moving business functions from the West Coast to metro Detroit.

thumbnail.caption: Mullen Automotive CEO David Michery with Bollinger B4 electric truck at Bollinger's Oak Park, Mich., headquarters.

content.title: Mullen CEO David Michery doubles down on commercial EVs after buying out Bollinger
content.summary: Mullen CEO David Michery is undeterred by the soft demand for commercial EVs. He plans to dramatically ramp up production of the B4 chassis cab electric truck.

thumbnail.caption: Mullen Automotive CEO David Michery, at Bollinger's Oak Park, Mich., headquarters, believes the difficult market for EVs is temporary. His strategy is to wait out the tariff negotiations while positioning Mullen Automotive and Bollinger Motors for big production increases.
